title.rendered: There Is Now No Condemnation: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The verdict has already been given, not guilty. Romans 8:1 is not a goal to reach. It is the truth about you right now, in Christ Jesus. No condemnation. Not after you improve. Now.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, May 5, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
Romans 8:1 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

One word carries the full weight of this verse: now. Not after you improve. Not when you get your act together. Not once you have gone long enough without failing. Now. Right now. In Christ Jesus, there is no condemnation.

The accuser wants you to live in the courtroom, always on trial, always defending yourself, always waiting for the verdict. But the verdict has already been given. Romans 8:1 is the verdict. No condemnation. Case closed. The Judge who has all authority looked at your life, looked at the cross, and declared: not guilty. In Christ.

This is not a license to sin, Paul addresses that directly as he continues in Romans 8:1–4. It is freedom to live. The person who knows they are not condemned does not live carelessly, they live freely. Freely loved, freely forgiven, freely empowered to walk not according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

Condemnation paralyses. Grace activates. You may have failed yesterday. The answer is not to wallow in guilt until you feel sufficiently punished. The answer is Romans 8:1. In Christ, right now, there is no condemnation. Receive it. Rise from it. Walk in it.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I receive the freedom of Romans 8:1 today. I refuse the condemnation the enemy wants me to carry. I am in Christ Jesus and there is no condemnation for me, not because I deserve it but because Jesus paid for it. I rise from guilt and walk in the freedom that grace provides. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

There is now no condemnation for me, I am in Christ Jesus. The verdict has been given and it is final: not guilty. I do not live in the courtroom of guilt and shame. I live in the freedom of grace. I am not condemned by my past, my failures, or my weaknesses. I am loved, forgiven and free, right now, in Christ.
